case_study.headline: A new templates library reached 928 Google clicks a month in 5 months
case_study.summary: Example Booking Software launched a library of free templates for salons, clinics and studios on 2026-04-15. In its first 5 full months it earned 2,375 clicks and 61,805 impressions in Google search, growing from 86 clicks in May to 928 in September, and visits that started there were followed by 64 sign-ups.
case_study.starting_point: A new section with no search traffic: /templates/ had 0 clicks in the 28 days before the launch (2026-03-18 to 2026-04-14).
what_was_done: 2026-04-15: the templates library launched at /templates/ with ready-to-use policies, reminder texts and forms.
2026-04-22: Templates linked from the main menu and the footer.
2026-07-13: 12 more templates added, linked from 20 blog posts.
2026-09-21: Page speed work across the whole site.

partial_month.note: partial month: shown separately, not compared with the full months

results_text: Clicks rose every month, from 86 in May to 928 in September, and impressions from 1,740 to 26,013; the average position improved from 14.4 to 9.9.
The rest of the site grew much more slowly: from May to September the section's clicks grew 10.8x against 1.1x for the rest of the site, and its share of page-level clicks went from 2% to 14%.
The 12 templates added on 2026-07-13 were followed by a 150% rise in clicks over the next 28 days, while the rest of the site moved 2%.
CTR fell from 4.9% to 3.6% as the pages began to show for broader searches.
GA4 recorded 2,427 sessions that started on the templates and 64 sign-ups from them, from 2 in May to 24 in September.
how_we_measured: Google Search Console, 2026-05-01 to 2026-09-30; data through 2026-10-25, so 2026-10 is partial and not compared.
Section = pages under /templates/; control = every other page, counted the same way (per page).
Queries are visible for 51% of the section's clicks; Google hides rare searches.
GA4 sessions starting on the section, all channels; sign-ups are the sign_up key event. GA4 passed the tracking check in all 5 months (organic sessions 0.86 to 0.89 times Search Console clicks).
The 2026-09-21 page speed work moved the whole site, so the section's gain after it is not credited to it.
case_study.whats_next: The open question is CTR, which fell as impressions grew. Next is new page titles on the 3 templates with the most impressions, which together bring 53% of the section's clicks; the new titles get their own before and after test once 14 days of data exist.

stage_1_permission_request.text: Hi, thanks for the kind words about your Google Ads last month. Would Example Family Dental share that story with other practices? It takes a short form (about 10 minutes) with the before and after numbers, then a 30-minute call, recorded only if you agree. You choose how you appear: the practice and your name, the practice and your role only, or no names at all. You'll see every quote and the full draft before anything is published, and you can pull out at any point until then. As a thank-you we'll waive one month of management fees. That doesn't depend on what you say, and we'll mention it next to your quote. Could we read the numbers in the Google Ads account we manage for you, to check them? Reply yes or no to each part.

case_study.headline: Example Family Dental booked 47% more new patients from Google Ads
case_study.summary: Example Family Dental, a family dental practice with 3 locations in the US Midwest, moved its Google Ads to Example Growth Agency on 2026-06-01 and kept the same budget. In July to September it booked 141 new patients from Google Ads, up from 96 in March to May, and each one cost $127 instead of $185.
case_study.the_customer: A family dental practice with 3 locations in the US Midwest and 11 dentists and hygienists. Its practice manager runs marketing alongside the front desk.
case_study.before: The practice spent about $5,940 a month on Google Ads but could not tie the spend to new patients. "Every Monday I'd open the Google Ads bill and have no idea what we got for it." Matching invoices to new patient forms took the practice manager's Friday afternoons, and still gave no answer.
case_study.why_they_chose: The practice was about to open on Saturday mornings and did not want to spend more on ads it could not measure. Another practice owner had told the manager she finally knew her cost per new patient. To keep the comparison fair, the practice and Example Growth Agency kept the budget the same: "We agreed to keep the same budget so the only thing changing was how it was run."
case_study.rollout: Example Growth Agency took over the account on 2026-06-01. Call tracking numbers and new campaigns were live by 2026-06-20, the front desk began asking every caller how they found the practice, and the old campaigns were paused for a week. In the manager's words, "June was messy." June is left out of the results for that reason.
case_study.results_text: From July to September, after the switch, the practice booked 141 new patients who found it through a Google ad, 47% more than the 96 it booked from March to May. Spend stayed level ($17,806 before, $17,977 after), so the cost per booked new patient fell from $185 to $127 (-31%). Google Ads conversions, which count calls and form leads rather than booked patients, rose 27%, and more of them turned into bookings (26% before, 30% after). One thing has not moved: implant enquiries are still slow. The practice also began opening on Saturday mornings at one location on 2026-08-01, during the after period.
case_study.advice_to_peers: "Fix your tracking before you judge any agency. Once the front desk asked every caller how they found us, the reports finally matched what we saw in the chairs."
case_study.quote: "Fix your tracking before you judge any agency.", Practice manager, Example Family Dental. Example Family Dental had one month of Example Growth Agency's management fees waived for taking part in this story.
case_study.how_we_measured: Booked new patients come from the practice's own software (its referral-source report), as given on the practice's form. Spend and conversions come from the practice's Google Ads account, pulled for the same dates with the practice's permission; the spend is 1.1% from its invoices for the before period and 0.1% for the after period. Both periods are 92 days. June, the rollout month, is left out. No control group exists, so these results followed the switch; other changes (the Saturday hours) are named above. This is one practice's result; it is not a figure for what every client gets.
